incident-bot: :rotating_light: Alert: elevated 5xx error rate detected for inference-prod (gateway). 502/504 spike starting 04:12 UTC. Paging oncall: @maya

maya (oncall): saw it, joining. looking at grafana now — thanks

incident-bot: summary: 5xx spikes correlate with model-runner segfaults and OOMs on nodes in us-west-2. error rate ~14% over last 3m. Affected route: /v1/generate (redwood-model-a)

maya (oncall): @igor can you grab logs for model-runner pools? I'm going to pause canary traffic to redwood-model-a to limit customer impact

igor: pulling logs from node infer-uw2-13 now. quick grep shows repeated segfault stack: `sigsegv` inside quant_attention.c at ~line 842. pattern: heavy long-seq requests (>8k tokens) seem to trigger

igor: relevant tail: ```
[04:09:11] model-runner[pid=4212]: kv_cache_alloc: size=1.2GB
[04:09:11] model-runner[pid=4212]: quant_attention: allocating kernel workspace
[04:09:12] model-runner[pid=4212]: segfault (signal 11)
[04:09:12] kernel: evicting process due to OOM
```

maya (oncall): thanks. i'm removing canary and enabling fallback routing to redwood-model-b (smaller model) — doing a config flip now

kevin: confirmed route change propagated to edge in ~30s. traffic to redwood-model-a dropped to ~5% for us-west, fallback to redwood-model-b at 95%

alice: customer-impact check: 3 enterprise customers reporting increased latencies and 502s, roughly 10-15% of their requests. creating incident page for customer comms

liz: running `kubectl logs --since=10m -n inference model-runner-4212 -c runner` shows recurrent OOM lines. may be memory leak under long context. attaching grep results

igor: copying core dump and stacktrace to /shared/incident/6219054321/. stack snippet: `#0 0x7f8d2c3a in quant_attn_forward+0x1a3`

maya (oncall): immediate mitigations enacted: 1) route fallback to smaller model 2) scale up dedicated pool for redwood-model-b +3 nodes 3) cordon suspect nodes (infer-uw2-12/13) to prevent further evictions

sre-bridge-bot: autoscaler: requested 3 additional gpu nodes in us-west-2 (pool: model-b-dedicated). ETA ~2m

kevin: adding a transient rate limit on /v1/generate for anonymous users (50rps) to reduce pressure. internal api keys exempted.

customer-support: logged initial customer impact notes and opened support tickets CUST-9421, CUST-9422. Asked customers to route critical requests to dedicated endpoints (if configured).

maya (oncall): trying a soft-restart of model-runner on infer-uw2-13 to get core dump uploaded for forensics: `systemctl restart model-runner@13`

igor: restart completed but node immediately OOM'd again under test replay. reproducer: replaying a 12k token request caused process to die within 8s.

maya (oncall): okay we need a hotfix or quick rollback. options: 1) apply kernel/memory limits to prevent huge allocations, 2) roll back to previous model-compilation artifact (v1.4 -> v1.3), 3) deploy a temporary quantization-safe build. Which is fastest?

igor: rollback to v1.3 is fastest. v1.4 introduced new attention kernel. v1.3 binaries are available and compatible with weights. I'll prepare rollout patch

liz: last-prod-deploy shows v1.4 rollout started 03:40 UTC for ~10% canary to redwood-model-a. it hit high mem tests at canary stage but auto-promoted due to false negative in perf test.

maya (oncall): ok proceed with rollback to v1.3 for redwood-model-a. coordinate canary -> full rollback. kevin coordinate routing and downtime windows

kevin: initiating rollback job: `deploy rollback redwood-model-a --to=1.3 --parallel=3` Started at 04:20 UTC. monitoring

sre-bridge-bot: deploy job started. canary stage 1/3.

igor: while rollback runs, continue to cordon nodes and collect core dumps. i uploaded heap maps to /shared/incident/6219054321/heapmaps.tar.gz

alice: customer comms draft: "We're investigating elevated 5xx errors on model endpoint in US-WEST. We've routed traffic to fallback model and are rolling back a recent runtime change. We'll update in 30 minutes." sending to legal for review

maya (oncall): handoff note (to night team): if rollback doesn't reduce 5xx to <1% in 15m, escalate to platform kernel team and consider pausing all long-context jobs (context>8k) via router filtering. tagging @igor for overnight followup

kevin: rollback completed at 04:27 UTC. Post-rollback metrics: 5xx dropped from 14% -> 1.2% in 5 minutes. latency returned close to baseline for most customers.

customer-support: notified impacted customers with initial update. tickets updated CUST-9421/CUST-9422. customers acknowledged and appreciate quick action

maya (oncall): good. leaving followups: - postmortem owner: @alice - root cause triage: @igor + eng-ml (quant kernels) - long-term: add mem-safety e2e test on long-contexts + improve canary perf tests - remediate: patch quant_attention to add allocation guardrails

alice: created incident doc: https://redwood.incidents/INC-6219054321 with timeline and customer impact. setting sev: high.

maya (oncall): handing off to @igor for overnight watch. I'm off in 30m. If errors reappear, escalate to platform-kernel and page oncall-sre. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:

igor: taking over. I'll validate core dumps and coordinate with eng-ml tomorrow. added note: keep fallback routing until kernel patch merged and validated.

sre-bridge-bot: incident status: mitigated -> monitoring. closed pager for maya. next update expected in 2h or on new alert. :white_check_mark:
